subject: chemistry-2
question: A hypothetical laboratory solution is reported to have a pH of 3. Which value correctly gives its hydronium ion concentration?
explanation:
Because pH = -log[H3O+], the concentration is recovered as [H3O+] = 10^-pH, so a pH of 3 gives 1 × 10^-3 mol/L. Option B is the hydroxide concentration of this same solution, since pOH = 14 - 3 = 11. Options A and C treat the digit 3 as a coefficient rather than as the exponent, a frequent error when converting between pH and concentration.

ELI-10: The pH value is an exponent, so undoing it means raising 10 to the negative of that number. A pH of 3 becomes 10^-3, which is 0.001 mol/L; the leading coefficient is 1, not 3. If the pH had been 3.5, the concentration would fall between 10^-4 and 10^-3, closer to 3 × 10^-4. Whenever a pH is a whole number, the concentration is a 1 sitting in that decimal place: pH 3 gives 0.001 and pH 5 gives 0.00001.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
